newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss liberalise rules for foreign bank branches.
newsitem.headline: Swiss liberalise rules for foreign bank branches.

text.p: The Swiss Federal Banking Commission has approved a new set of rules which it says liberalises existing regulations pertaining to branches of foreign banks in Switzerland.

A spokesman for the commission said the changes, effective January 1, 1997, will not affect many banks, as they apply only to branches of foreign banks and there are only about 15 of these in Switzerland. Most foreign banks have subsidiaries as opposed to branches.
The new rules replace existing regulations adopted in 1984, the Banking Commission said in a statement.
The rules also liberalise cross-border business. Foreign bank branches which accept funds from Swiss-based accounts will no longer be required to have explicit approval for such activities.
The changes will make it easier for branches to transfer money earned by foreign workers to bank accounts outside Switzerland, for example.
The rules include a provision allowing branches of foreign banks which meet certain criteria to calculate their year-end earnings and balance according to foreign regulations.
The new rules are in line with the principle whereby oversight of foreign banks is seen as mainly a function of the respective foreign regulator, the Banking Commission said.
The rules also will require reciprocal treatment of Swiss banks in the respective countries, it said.
